name: Italian Lemon Olive Oil Cake with Raspberries

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 350°F and place rack in the center position. Lightly oil a 9-inch cake or springform pan, then press a piece of parchment paper (cut to fit) into the bottom of the pan. Set aside.
Place sugar, oil, and vanilla in a medium bowl. Whisk until light yellow in color, about 1 minute.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ¼ cups granulated sugar
1 cup extra virgin olive oil
½ tsp vanilla extract

instructions.primary_message: Working over a small bowl, separate 1 egg yolk from the white, leaving the white in the bowl. Add yolk to the bowl with the sugar and whisk to combine. (Reserve egg white for another use.)
Add additional eggs to the bowl, one at a time, and whisk until each is fully incorporated.
Add buttermilk to the bowl and whisk until smooth.
Wash, dry, and zest 2 lemons. Juice lemons into a small bowl (you will need 6 tablespoons juice). If you are short on juice, juice the 3rd lemon to make up the difference.
Add 6 tablespoons lemon juice to the medium bowl, along with salt, baking powder, and baking soda. Whisk vigorously until fully combined.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp baking powder
½ tsp baking soda

instructions.primary_message: Add flour to the bowl and whisk once more to combine the batter (be careful not to overmix).

Pour batter into the prepared cake pan. Place pan in the oven and bake, undisturbed, until cake is cooked through (the top should be slightly domed and firm to the touch when pressed gently in the center), 45-50 minutes. Remove from oven and let cool completely.

Once the cake has cooled, run a knife around the edges of the cake and remove from the pan. Peel away the parchment paper and transfer the cake to a serving platter. Sift powdered sugar over the top of the cake.
To serve, wash and dry raspberries. Slice cake into wedges and serve with a handful of raspberries on the side. Enjoy!
